newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firm on monopolies tax payments, rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firm on monopolies tax payments, rate cut.

text.p: The rouble was firm on Thursday as major bank clients sought funds to pay tax arrears and dealers said today's refinancing rate cut encouraged banks to invest in government securities more actively.
The central bank is cutting its refinancing rate to 36 percent with effect from April 28 from the 42 percent in force since February 10.
roubles/dollar Apr 24 midday Apr 24 early Apr 23 close
"The rouble is doing well against the dollar under pressure from clients as natural monopolies are being urged to pay taxes," Aljba Alliance Bank chief dealer Dmitry Slobodnik said.
The authorities are putting pressure on monopolies such as the natural gas and power generation industries, which have no competitors, to restructure and pay their tax arrears.
Dealers said gas monopoly Gazprom was buying roubles quite actively.
They added the refinancing rate cut was a psychological support for the rouble, as it heralds a further decline in Treasury bill yields.
"People are feeling that the central bank will give them no gift of yields so they prefer to sell dollars to buy T-bills now," one said.
Another dealer said commercial banks also needed funds to square month-end balance-sheets ahead of Russia's May Day and Victory Day holidays.
